title: Onboarding digest and deterministic pin ID generator for ephemeral variants
creator: Evan Brooks
description:
Problem: onboarding new third-party and research models creates a burst of near-duplicate variant IDs and inconsistent metadata artifacts (manifest.json, perf profiles, README snippets). This leads to flaky pin references, unclear rollback behavior, and duplicated engineering effort when publishing compact performance bundles for hosted and Dedicated customers.

Goal: implement a small 'onboarding digest' generator that produces a normalized metadata digest (human summary + machine signature) and a deterministic short pin ID generator that is stable across transient ingest differences (e.g., whitespace, attribute ordering, non-semantic fields). Update docs/templates and the model-catalog publish flow to attach the digest and pin ID to every staged publish.

Success criteria: reproducible pin IDs across re-ingests of the same model artifacts, consistent compact perf bundle attachments, and reduced support tickets about 'missing pin' or 'variant mismatch' by 80% within the next quarter.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A CLI/CI step 'redwood catalog digest' produces the same digest and 8-char pin ID for identical canonical inputs across runs.
2) The staging publish includes the digest and references the generated pin ID in the manifest and the catalog UI.
3) Perf profile publishing links the compact perf bundle to the digest and is discoverable via the console.
4) Integration tests added to the ingest pipeline cover whitespace/ordering shuffles and return the same pin ID.
5) Documentation pages and quickstart examples updated with the new workflow and example outputs.
implementation_notes:
Design choices considered:
- Use canonical JSON (RFC8785/CANONICAL_JSON) vs. protobuf hashing. Chosen: canonical JSON with deterministic key sort and removal of known non-semantic fields (ingest_timestamp, source_url_hash).
- Hash function: Blake3-256 truncated to 16 hex chars then base58-encode trimmed to 8 chars for readable pins. Rationale: fast, stable, low-collision risk for our catalog size.
- Backward compatibility: existing pinned model references will continue to resolve; new generator will produce a new field 'deterministic_pin' while preserving legacy 'pin_hash' to allow phased migration.

Implementation tasks:
- Add catalog/digest library (go/python): normalizer, field-blacklist, canonicalizer, blake3 wrapper.
- CI job to run on PRs under 'catalog-ingest' that verifies digest stability.
- Small console change to display digest and provide copy-to-clipboard short pin.
- Update model ingestion lambda to attach deterministic_pin to manifest and catalog index.
- Publish migration script to backfill deterministic_pin for recent 30 days of ingests with idempotent semantics.

Estimated effort per component: library (2d), CI integration (1d), ingest change (1d), console (1d), backfill script (1d).
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: (canary) Enable digest generation in staging for a subset of models (internal and research ingest) and run backfill on a test index. Monitor mismatches and collisions.
Phase 2: Enable for all staging publishes; surface deterministic_pin in console but do not make it authoritative for routing.
Phase 3: After 1 week without issues, begin including deterministic_pin in hosted API responses as 'pin_id' for new publishes and allow routing by pin_id with fallback to legacy pins.
Phase 4: Offer opt-in migration for Dedicated customers to switch to deterministic pin routing.
Rollback: Remove deterministic_pin from manifest and revert ingest pipeline to previous commit. Backfill operations are idempotent; older manifests remain unchanged.
testing_plan:
Unit tests for canonicalizer and hashing with >30 fixtures including ordering/whitespace/noise.
Integration test: ingest pipeline job that asserts identical canonical digest across simulated re-ingest variations.
Load test: ensure digest generation adds <10ms per manifest at 95th percentile under normal ingest concurrency.
Collision test: generate deterministic pins for a synthetic dataset of 200k variant manifests and assert collision rate is <1 in 10M.
E2E: staging publish, console display, perf bundle attachment, and API retrieval validated by automation.
Monitoring: catalog-metrics:pin_generation_latency, pin_collision_alerts (counter), manifest-mismatch-rate.
